name: Iscah
overview: Iscah is a female figure mentioned in the Bible as the daughter of Haran. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about her tribe or other personal notes. Her brief mention situates her within the early genealogical records of Genesis.
namesAndTitles: The name Iscah appears only once in Scripture, in Genesis 11:29, with no specific meaning or divine origin indicated. Therefore, her name is presented plainly without further etymological insight.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Iscah as the daughter of Haran, establishing a direct family relationship. No other familial connections or relationships are recorded in the biblical text concerning her.
scriptureSignificance: Iscah's significance lies in her inclusion among the descendants of Terah, providing a link in the genealogical lineage that leads to key patriarchal figures. Although her role is not elaborated upon, her mention helps to preserve the historical and familial context within the Genesis narrative. This brief record underscores the faithfulness of Scripture in documenting even lesser-known individuals who contribute to God's unfolding plan.
